inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2-1.3 gives a cost of equity of 10.2-10.7%; debt is <0.5% of EV so WACC ~10.0%. Held at 10.0% in ALL THREE scenarios: memory-cycle risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate (owner-fcf-adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost is expensed inside COGS/opex and therefore already charged within the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities are immaterial (<1% of the cash pile) and are not added to debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - no material non-controlling interest. Equity-method income ($59m FY26) is ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (cyclical operating company) with owner-fcf-adaptations applied: risk charged once in the flows, single lease treatment, matching-asset rule (interest income stripped, cash added once). FRESH BUILD - no prior DCF or Drivers file. CYCLE POSITION: FY26 is the steepest up-cycle in memory history (revenue 3.6x, GAAP gross margin 80.7%, Q4 run-rate $217bn/yr, FQ1-27 guided $61.5bn at ~86% GM). Revenue is running at ~6-8x the cash cost base against a FY18 peak of 2.7x and a FY14-25 average EBITDA margin of 42%, so NOTHING in the latest year is carried forward: every forecast year is built from components with the FY27 guidance year anchored to the 30 Sept guidance and FY28+ set by judgment on where revenue/cost settles once clean rooms built now yield bits (late 2028+). 10-year horizon because margins only mature after the FY29-31 normalisation. CUSTOMER DEPOSITS: $12,895m noncurrent customer contract liabilities (take-or-pay Strategic Customer Agreements, 26 agreements, ~35% of bit volume through 2030) are deducted in the bridge as debt-like - the cash is in the pile and the revenue it prepays is in the projections. A further ~$18bn of deposits is contracted but not yet received and is NOT added. TAX: GAAP ETR 14.8% (Pillar Two 15% floor, Singapore); other noncurrent liabilities carry ~$5.8bn+ of deferred income-tax payable at Q3, so FY27 cash tax rate is set at 18% to absorb the FY26 catch-up, 16% thereafter (Pillar Two floor plus a rising US share from the Idaho fabs). DATA: the XBRL quarter labels in the Metrics CSV are shifted one quarter late ('Q4 2025' rev 13,643 is really Q1 FY26; 'Q2 2026' 41,456 is Q3 FY26; H1-2026 = 13,643 + 23,860 ties). FY26 totals and the FY-end balance sheet are taken from the 30 Sept 2026 8-K EX-99.1 because the 10-K is not yet filed. Price is the 1 Oct regular close; to be replaced by refresh_price.py.

equity_bridge.item: Customer deposits under Strategic Customer Agreements (debt-like prepaid revenue)
equity_bridge.note: Noncurrent customer contract liabilities at 3 Sep 2026 (8-K EX-99.1 balance sheet; $142m a year earlier). Cash received is in the $73.5bn pile; the bits it prepays are in projected revenue, so the liability is deducted to avoid counting the same cash twice.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case mid-cycle trend (FY32-FY36 revenue growth, bits +15-20%/yr against long-run price/bit declines). Every trailing CAGR is a trough-to-peak artefact and unusable as a forward proxy.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All trailing CAGRs are measured from the FY23 trough (revenue $15.5bn, loss of $5.8bn) or the FY21 mid-cycle to the FY26 super-peak and diverge from each other and from any sustainable rate by far more than 30%. EPS and owner-FCF 3-yr CAGRs are undefined (negative FY23 base: EPS -5.34, owner FCF ~-6.7bn). FY16-FY26 10-yr revenue CAGR 26.8% and the FY18-peak-to-FY26-peak rate of 20.3%/yr are also cycle-inflated.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC incl. withholding less interest income): FY21 ~1.9bn, FY22 ~2.5bn, FY23 ~-6.7bn, FY24 ~-1.0bn, FY25 ~0.1bn, FY26 58.8bn. Cumulative FY15-FY25 reported FCF was only ~$15bn on ~$262bn of revenue (5.8%) - the through-cycle cash economics of memory before this cycle. The forward build assumes a structurally better mid-cycle than that history (SCA floors, HBM/data-centre mix, three-player DRAM oligopoly) but far below FY26-27.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +84% to ~$245bn: FQ1-27 guided $61.5bn with 'single-digit sequential bit growth', 75% of FY27 shipments already allocated/contracted, HBM pricing reset higher for CY27; held roughly flat across the year rather than compounding Q1. FY28 -6%: bits +12%, pricing begins to roll as the first new industry clean rooms and the CY27 HBM/CPU digestion arrive. FY29-31 -22/-20/-8 (cumulative -41%): the supply response built in FY26-28 (Micron construction capex alone rising for late-2028 clean rooms; Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT likewise) meets a hyperscaler capex digestion; sits between the FY18-20 (-30%) and FY22-23 (-50%) busts, softened by SCA floors on ~35% of bits. FY32-36 +5-6%: bits +15-20%/yr against long-run price/bit declines, i.e. the memory industry's through-cycle revenue trend of 5-8%.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 86%: guided GM ~86%, opex ~$2.3bn/qtr (3.8%), D&A ~4.9% added back. FY28 82%: pricing softens faster than the cost base. FY29-31 74/64/58: revenue falls toward 2.3-2.5x cash cost. Mid-cycle 57-58%: ABOVE the FY14-25 average (42%) and the FY18 peak (65% in that year) because (i) SCA floor prices on ~35% of bits are stated to yield GM 'well above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle' (>61%) through 2030, (ii) HBM/data-centre mix, (iii) three-player DRAM discipline; but BELOW anything the market is extrapolating from 87% today. D&A climbs from 7% to 17.5% of revenue as the $30-45bn/yr FY26-28 capex depreciates over a smaller revenue base; capex intensity settles at 22% (half the FY19-25 average of ~40%, because the structural revenue base is larger relative to equipment cost, and because D&A < capex is needed for 6% growth). Working capital: receivables + inventory far exceed payables (FY26: -$18.5bn on +$95.8bn revenue), so growth consumes ~12% of the revenue change and the FY29-31 decline releases it.
base.narrative: Peak-and-normalise. The AI build-out keeps memory sold out through FY28, Micron banks ~$240bn of owner FCF over FY27-28, then industry supply and a hyperscaler digestion bring a classic memory down-cycle in FY29-31 that bottoms well above any past trough because of SCA floors and HBM mix. The company that emerges is roughly FY26-sized in revenue by FY34 with 57-58% EBITDA margins, 22% capex intensity and ~27% owner-FCF margins - a far better business than the FY15-25 one, but a cyclical commodity producer capitalised at 13x mid-cycle FCF, not a software compounder.

bull.narrative: Durable supercycle. Management's 'no line of sight to when supply and demand balances' proves right: HBM trade ratios (HBM4E) and diminishing node returns cap industry bit growth, agentic AI workloads and CPU-attached memory keep demand compounding, SCAs extend beyond 2030 at ceilings reset to today's pricing, and Micron holds its ~25% DRAM share into custom HBM4E with NVIDIA. Revenue peaks near $285bn in FY28, the FY29-31 air-pocket is only -22% cumulative, and the business plateaus as a 68%-EBITDA-margin oligopolist growing 7%/yr - memory re-rated from commodity to AI infrastructure. This is approximately what today's price capitalises.

bear.narrative: The cycle does what memory cycles have always done. Pricing rolls over in H2 FY27 as hyperscaler capex growth stalls and customers that bought ahead at 4-5x prices work down inventory; Samsung, SK Hynix and CXMT add bits aggressively into FY28-29; Micron loses HBM4E allocation to the two larger HBM suppliers; the 65% of uncontracted volume reprices down 60-70% (as in 2022-23) and some SCA counterparties push to renegotiate floors. Revenue falls 49% peak-to-trough (FY28 $229bn to FY30 $88bn), EBITDA margin troughs at 32% (above FY23's 13% because of the floors), and the business settles at its historical 42% mid-cycle margin with 26% capex intensity - the FY15-25 economics on a larger base. Owner FCF in the trough years is near zero; FY27-28 still deliver ~$185bn.

scenario_narratives.base: Peak-and-normalise: FY27-28 at ~$245bn/86-82% margins (guidance-anchored), a 41% three-year revenue bust in FY29-31 as 2026-28 clean-room capex yields bits into an AI-capex digestion, then a structurally better mid-cycle (57-58% EBITDA margin vs a 42% FY14-25 average) because SCA floors cover ~35% of bits through 2030 and HBM/data-centre mix is permanent. Valued as a cyclical at 13x mid-cycle FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Durable supercycle: structurally constrained supply (HBM trade ratios, diminishing node returns, multi-year clean-room lead times) plus compounding agentic-AI demand keeps the market tight through 2030; SCAs extend and reset higher; revenue plateaus near $230-310bn at 66-68% margins. The market price today roughly equals this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: Classic memory bust from H2 FY27: inventory digestion, competitor bit growth, HBM4E share loss and floor renegotiations take revenue down 49% to FY30 with a 32% trough margin; the business reverts to its 42% historical mid-cycle margin at 26% capex intensity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear UP to 25%: memory has followed every up-cycle with a bust for forty years (FY12, FY16, FY19-20, FY23), FY26 margins are 2x any past peak, and a hyperscaler AI-capex digestion is a single macro event that would hit 60%+ of revenue at once. Bull DOWN to 25%: it requires several independent things to hold simultaneously - AI capex compounding through 2030, no effective supply response from Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT despite record industry capex, SCA ceilings/floors surviving a soft market, and Micron keeping HBM share into custom HBM4E. Symmetric weights around a base that already sits far above the company's own through-cycle history.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A memory maker is valued on its mid-cycle owner FCF plus the present value of the super-normal cash it banks before the cycle turns, never on the peak-year run-rate. FY26-27 are the peak: revenue is 6-8x cash cost against a 2.7x prior record, and the market capitalisation (~$1.26tn) is roughly 7x FY27 earnings - which is the market itself saying a steep decline follows. The DCF therefore spends its effort on (i) how much cash arrives in FY27-28 (anchored to guidance, ~$240bn owner FCF in the base), (ii) how deep and how long the FY29-31 normalisation is, and (iii) what mid-cycle margin the SCAs, HBM mix and oligopoly structure make durable. House basis expenses SBC including the withholding paid on vested shares; interest income is stripped and the cash pile added once; the $12.9bn of customer deposits is treated as prepaid revenue (debt-like). Terminal value capped at 11-14x mid-cycle FCF, the range a buyer pays for a cyclical commodity producer.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing and depth: a one-year delay in the FY29 downturn adds ~$100bn of owner FCF (~$75/share after discounting); an earlier or deeper bust (bear) removes it. The base's -41% cumulative decline is a judgment, not a forecast.

Mid-cycle margin: each 5pp on the FY32-36 EBITDA margin is worth roughly $60-70/share through the terminal value. The 57-58% base rests on SCA floors (35% of bits, >61% GM) that have never been tested in a down-market.
Terminal multiple: 13x mid-cycle FCF vs 11x or 15x moves base value by ~+/-$55/share; the market today pays what is effectively a growth multiple on peak FCF.

Working-capital and tax unwind: FY26 OCF benefited from ~$8bn of deferred income tax (noncurrent taxes payable) and receivables ballooned to $36bn; both reverse in FY27-29 and are only approximated here (18% FY27 cash tax, -12% WC capture).
Capex escalation: FY27 capex is guided up (construction for late-2028 clean rooms) without a number; every $5bn/yr above the modelled ~$39-42bn is ~$4/share per year.
Geopolitics: US export controls and China's exclusion of Micron from critical infrastructure (CXMT/YMTC gaining) are priced through the share assumptions only indirectly.
Price volatility: the stock has moved 179.61-1255.00 in 52 weeks; the Yahoo close is a point estimate and the upside figures move daily.

sanity_check_note.why_no_methodology_fix: The diagnosis candidates are 'peak_fcf' and 'wacc_too_low'. The build already does not extrapolate the FY26 FCF: base owner FCF falls from $120bn (FY27) to $36-47bn mid-cycle and the bear case to $6-10bn, and the FY29-31 bust is explicit in the growth paths. A WACC premium would charge cyclicality a second time on top of the scenario flows and 25% bear weight (owner-fcf-adaptations section f) and would not pass the check anyway: against FY25 earnings a 36x P/E ceiling implies <= $269/share, below the bear case. Re-run the check after the FY2026 10-K is extracted (expected mid-October 2026); it should pass without any change to the drivers.
